medications.drug: 3 ML insulin glargine 100 UNT/ML Pen Injector
medications.sig: Inject 20 units under the skin at bedtime

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Repeat A1c this morning 7.9 (7.8 in November, before the steroid burst). Fasting sugars on her meter since the taper ended: 150s to 170s. Confirms type 2 diabetes.

Face keeps improving; ENT pleased at the 2 week check.

Talked through options at length: she is on prednisone indefinitely, which drives a lot of the sugar, and after watching her glucose climb on the high-dose course she would rather take one injection at night than start pills and add more later. She is comfortable with a pen after the hospital teaching. Reasonable choice.

Plan: insulin glargine 20 units at bedtime. Fasting checks daily, low sugar symptoms and treatment reviewed, glucagon not needed at this dose. Diabetes education referral offered, she will read the materials first. Eye exam with her optometrist this spring. Foot exam today: pulses 2+, monofilament intact, skin intact.
Recheck A1c in 3 months.

documents.title: Sugar numbers
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Three weeks on the glargine. Fasting this week: 128, 134, 119, 141, 125, 122, 130. No lows. Is that ok or should I go up?

documents.title: RE: Sugar numbers
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Those look good. Stay at 20 units. Let me know if you see anything under 70.

documents.title: Pen needles and test strips
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Insurance rejected 32G pen needles quantity over plan limit and requested PA for test strips (once daily testing). PA submitted with diagnosis of type 2 diabetes on basal insulin. Approved same afternoon for 12 months. Pharmacy notified.

conditions.label: Herpes zoster oticus (Ramsay Hunt syndrome), right

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM f/u. A1c 7.2, down from 7.9 on glargine 20. Fasting mostly 110s to 130s, no hypoglycemia.
Ramsay Hunt: right face almost back. Slight asymmetry of the smile when tired, eye closes fully, taste normal. ENT discharged her from routine follow-up.
TN quiet on carbamazepine.
Exam: BP at goal. Face near-symmetric at rest, mild weakness at the right corner of the mouth on full smile. Heart, lungs normal. Feet normal.
Plan: same insulin. Urine albumin, MTX labs today. Eye exam booked next month. Back in 3 months.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination (05/14/2018)
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Optometry report
Exam date: 05/14/2018
VA 20/20 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. IOP 15/16. Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, no macular edema. Lens clear. Right lid closure complete.
Recommendation: annual dilated exam.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Garden in full swing, picking beans daily. Sugars steady. Taking insulin every night.
A1c pending at time of visit; in range last time.
BP ok. Exam: lungs clear, heart regular, feet warm and intact, no edema.
Continue. Return October with flu shot.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine left deltoid. Tolerated without issue. She mentioned feeling run down lately; has appointment with PCP 10/29.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About two months of abdominal bloating and feeling full after half a meal. Waistbands tight. No pain, no vomiting, bowels a little slow, no blood. No vaginal bleeding; periods stopped this past spring. Also more tired again and cold all the time over the summer and fall, like 2015. Has her endocrinology follow-up already booked for 12/10.
O: BP 140/86. Weight about the same. Abdomen mildly distended, soft, nontender, possible fullness in the right lower quadrant, no clear fluid wave. Pelvic exam: vague right adnexal fullness, nontender. No lymphadenopathy. Skin dry.
A: Bloating and early satiety in a postmenopausal woman with a possible adnexal fullness; needs pelvic imaging and CA-125 now. Hypothyroid symptoms back; endocrinology in six weeks.
P: Pelvic ultrasound this week, CA-125, CBC, CMP today. Will call with results. Return precautions for pain, vomiting, or bleeding.

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal imaging. Uterus 7.8 cm, homogeneous myometrium, endometrium 4 mm. Right adnexa: complex solid and cystic mass measuring 9.4 x 7.6 x 7.1 cm with internal vascularity on color Doppler. Left ovary not separately seen. Small volume free fluid in the pelvis consistent with ascites.
reports.conclusion: Complex solid and cystic right adnexal mass, 9.4 cm, with small volume ascites, suspicious for ovarian neoplasm. CT and gynecologic oncology evaluation recommended.

orders.order: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Renee with the ultrasound: 9 cm complex mass on the right ovary with a little fluid, and CA-125 486. Told her plainly this is worrying for ovarian cancer and that the next steps are a CT scan this week and a gynecologic oncologist. She was quiet but asked good questions. CT booked Thursday. Will call her when it's read and have the referral ready. Offered to see her in person anytime this week.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Large complex cystic and solid right adnexal mass, about 9.5 cm. Nodular soft tissue thickening of the omentum. Small ascites. Liver without focal lesion. Spleen, pancreas, adrenals normal. Kidneys enhance symmetrically without hydronephrosis. No retroperitoneal or pelvic adenopathy by size criteria. Lung bases clear. Bones without destructive lesion.
reports.conclusion: Right adnexal mass with omental nodularity and small ascites, compatible with primary ovarian malignancy with peritoneal spread.

documents.title: CT result and referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed CT with her: the ovarian mass plus nodules in the fatty apron over the bowel and some fluid. Most likely ovarian cancer that has spread within the abdomen, which surgeons often still treat with the aim of removing everything. Urgent gyn onc referral sent with images; their nurse called back, consult 11/20. She will bring a friend. Will send a note to her endocrinologist about the upcoming surgery.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology consultation (visit 11/20/2018)
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Outside gynecologic oncology service
Date of visit: 11/20/2018

Thank you for referring Ms. Duffy, 54, with a right adnexal mass, CA-125 486 and CT showing omental nodularity and small ascites.

She has had two months of bloating and early satiety. Background: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, RA on methotrexate and prednisone 5 mg, hypothyroidism, trigeminal neuralgia on carbamazepine, type 2 diabetes on glargine. Previous right facial nerve decompression. No drug allergies. A maternal aunt had premenopausal breast cancer.

Exam: performance status 0. Abdomen mildly distended, no palpable omental cake. Pelvic exam: firm mobile right adnexal mass. No supraclavicular nodes.

Impression: presumed advanced epithelial ovarian cancer, appropriate for primary cytoreductive surgery.

Plan: exploratory laparotomy, total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy and cytoreduction, scheduled 12/18. Perioperative steroid coverage and insulin plan with anesthesia. Genetic counseling and germline testing will be offered for all patients with epithelial ovarian cancer.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily, 30 minutes before breakfast

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up (visit 12/10/2018)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Date of visit: 12/10/2018

Ms. Duffy returns for her hypothyroidism. Over roughly half a year the fatigue, weight creep, constipation and constant chill have come back; she says she feels cold all day even with the heat up. She takes levothyroxine 75 mcg properly. Since we last saw her she has started carbamazepine for trigeminal neuralgia and insulin glargine for new type 2 diabetes. She is scheduled for surgery on 12/18 for a newly found ovarian mass.

Pulse 58, BP 142/88. Skin dry. Non-pitting puffiness around both eyes. Thyroid not palpable.

Labs today: TSH 12.5, free T4 0.7, total cholesterol 245, triglycerides 220.

Assessment: undertreated primary hypothyroidism. Carbamazepine speeds levothyroxine clearance and may well explain the higher requirement.

Plan: increase levothyroxine to 112 mcg daily, starting now; it is fine to continue around surgery and to resume as soon as she is taking pills. TSH in 8 weeks. Lipids should be rechecked once euthyroid. We will see her in 6 months.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of ovary
conditions.note: high-grade serous carcinoma, right ovary, FIGO IIIC; optimal cytoreduction 12/18/2018

procedures.procedure: Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy and cytoreduction

reports.text: Specimens: uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes and ovaries; omentum; peritoneal nodules. Right ovary: high-grade serous carcinoma, 9.6 cm, surface involvement present. Left ovary and both fallopian tubes: microscopic foci of high-grade serous carcinoma. Omentum: metastatic high-grade serous carcinoma, largest deposit 3.1 cm. Peritoneal nodules, pelvic: metastatic carcinoma. Uterus: inactive endometrium, no carcinoma; cervix unremarkable. Immunostains: WT1 positive, PAX8 positive, p53 aberrant (null pattern). Peritoneal washings positive for malignant cells.
reports.conclusion: High-grade serous carcinoma of ovarian origin, FIGO stage IIIC (pT3c).

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (12/18/2018 - 12/23/2018)
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Outside hospital, gynecologic oncology service
Admitted 12/18/2018, discharged 12/23/2018

Procedure 12/18: exploratory laparotomy, total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, infracolic omentectomy, resection of pelvic peritoneal nodules. Optimal cytoreduction with no gross residual disease. EBL 450 mL. No transfusion.

Course: stress-dose steroids then back to prednisone 5 mg. Glucose managed with glargine plus correction insulin, back to home glargine 20 units at discharge. Levothyroxine resumed at the new 112 mcg dose on day 2. Diet advanced on day 3. Incision clean.

Pathology: high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, FIGO IIIC.

Discharge medications: home regimen unchanged; acetaminophen as needed for incisional pain.
Follow-up: gynecologic oncology in 2 weeks to plan carboplatin and paclitaxel; genetic counseling referral placed. PCP visit in 1 to 2 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three weeks after laparotomy and debulking for stage IIIC high-grade serous ovarian cancer; surgeons got everything visible. Pathology reviewed with her today. Starts carboplatin and paclitaxel next Monday, every 3 weeks for 6 cycles. Using acetaminophen once a day for the incision. Eating smaller meals, bowels moving. Genetic counselor appointment next week.
Sugars 120s to 160s. Thyroid dose now 112.
Mood: scared but practical, has friends lined up for rides.
Exam: midline incision healed well, no erythema. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender. No calf tenderness.
A/P: post-op recovering well. Diabetes: chemo premedication with dexamethasone will push sugars up on infusion days; may add correction or adjust glargine with oncology, call with readings over 300. MTX: confirm plan with rheum and onc. Phone check in 2 weeks, visit April.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 8 hours as needed for nausea

documents.title: Medical oncology update (01/21/2019)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside gynecologic oncology / medical oncology
Date: 01/21/2019

Ms. Duffy received cycle 1 of carboplatin AUC 5 and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on 01/14/2019 and returns for a toxicity check. Mild nausea day 2 and 3, myalgias, fatigue. Glucose rose to the high 200s the day after dexamethasone premedication and settled by day 4. No fever.

Germline genetic testing: no pathogenic variant in BRCA1 or BRCA2 or the other genes on the panel.

Plan: continue every 3 weeks for 6 cycles. Ondansetron 4 mg every 8 hours as needed for nausea prescribed. Hair loss expected. CA-125 each cycle; CT after cycle 6. Thank you for monitoring her diabetes and thyroid.

documents.title: TSH
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH 2.1 on 112 mcg, good. Sodium and kidney function fine. Sent to endocrinology.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up (visit 03/18/2019)
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 03/18/2019

RA remains quiet through her chemotherapy for ovarian cancer; no synovitis today. We discussed methotrexate with her oncologist; counts have held, and both of us are comfortable continuing methotrexate 15 mg weekly and prednisone 5 mg with monitoring at your office. No change. Next visit in about two years unless she flares.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Five cycles done, last one 4/29. Tired, bald and wears a soft cap, but walking daily. Appetite low, weight down about 4 kg since January. Nausea controlled with ondansetron a day or two after each cycle.
Sugars: run 250s for two days after the steroid premed, otherwise 120s to 140s. A1c 7.6.
Oncology draws her counts each cycle, all ok to treat.
Exam: thin, no distress. BP 128/78. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, incision fine. No edema.
Plan: keep glargine 20; no changes while chemo winds down. Urine albumin today. Eye exam deferred to fall. Visit August.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Post hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and omentectomy. No ascites. No peritoneal nodularity. No adenopathy. Liver, spleen, kidneys normal. Chest portion of the study (separately reported) without nodules or effusion.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of residual or recurrent disease.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up (06/17/2019)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology
Date: 06/17/2019

Completed six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel on 04/29/2019. Mild residual fatigue, hair regrowing. Restaging CT chest/abdomen/pelvis on 06/10 shows no evidence of disease. CA-125 14 U/mL.

Plan: surveillance with exam and CA-125 every 3 months. No maintenance therapy given negative germline testing and her preference. Next visit September.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feeling stronger since finishing chemo in April; June CT clear. Short hair back. Weight 67, lowest she has been in years; eating normally now.
Sugars a bit lower without the premeds, no lows.
Exam: well appearing. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Feet: pulses intact, monofilament normal.
Continue all. MTX labs, A1c today. Mammogram due October.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up (09/16/2019)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology
Date: 09/16/2019

CA-125 has risen to 96 U/mL. CT shows several new peritoneal nodules up to 1.4 cm in the pelvis and along the right paracolic gutter. Recurrence under five months after platinum: platinum-resistant disease.

We discussed options and goals. She will begin pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 40 mg/m2 every 4 weeks. Hand-foot and mouth care reviewed. Ondansetron as before. CA-125 monthly, imaging after two cycles.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu shot right deltoid. Oncology okayed timing between doxorubicin cycles. No issues.

reports.text: Bilateral standard views. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No mass, suspicious calcification or distortion. Stable.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up (11/18/2019)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology
Date: 11/18/2019

After two cycles of liposomal doxorubicin the CA-125 has continued upward and CT shows growth of the peritoneal implants. Progression. Switching to gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 days 1 and 8 every 21 days. Counts and liver tests adequate. She remains active, ECOG 1.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cancer came back in September; doxorubicin didn't hold it and she is now on gemcitabine. Tired for 2 to 3 days after each dose. Frank about it: wants to keep trying treatments while she feels this well.
Sugars ok, glargine unchanged. No lows.
TN quiet. Thyroid symptoms gone on 112.
Exam: BP at goal. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no ascites by exam. No edema.
Plan: A1c, TSH, lipids today. Continue current meds. Offered to talk about advance care planning when she is ready; she'd like to next visit.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up (01/27/2020)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology
Date: 01/27/2020

CA-125 212 U/mL and CT with enlarging peritoneal disease after three cycles of gemcitabine: further progression. We discussed a fourth line. Plan vinorelbine 25 mg/m2 weekly, first dose 02/07/2020. Neuropathy, constipation and low counts discussed. Goals of care conversation documented; she wishes to continue active treatment.

documents.title: Patient call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt reports tingling and burning in toes and fingertips starting about 2 days after her new infusion on Friday, spreading up toward ankles. Saw oncology yesterday, who stopped the new drug. Some trouble with stairs. No breathing trouble, no bladder or bowel changes, can walk. Asked her to call 911 for any trouble breathing or swallowing or if she cannot walk. PCP aware.

documents.title: Oncology visit (02/10/2020)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology
Date of visit: 02/10/2020

Ms. Duffy, 56, with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma diagnosed 14 months ago, treated with optimal cytoreductive surgery and carboplatin/paclitaxel, then progression through liposomal doxorubicin and gemcitabine. She received her first dose of vinorelbine three days ago. Over the last 48 hours she has developed tingling, numbness and burning in the toes and fingertips, steadily moving upward. She has mild difficulty climbing stairs, feels generally worn out and is shedding more hair. Other history: RA on methotrexate and prednisone, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes on glargine, hypothyroidism, trigeminal neuralgia on carbamazepine, prior right Ramsay Hunt syndrome. No drug allergies. Former smoker.

Afebrile, vital signs stable.
Neuro: pinprick and vibration reduced in a stocking-and-glove distribution; mild weakness of both hip flexors; ankle jerks slightly diminished; upper limb strength normal. Breathing comfortable.
Abdomen: healed surgical scars, nontender, no organomegaly.
Labs: CBC, renal function and electrolytes normal.

Assessment: acute toxic polyneuropathy after vinorelbine.

Plan: vinorelbine discontinued permanently. Close observation; she knows to go to the emergency department for breathing or swallowing difficulty or inability to walk.  Reassess in 1 to 2 weeks; next line to be chosen avoiding neurotoxic agents.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up (03/09/2020)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology
Date: 03/09/2020

Neuropathy improving: hip flexor strength back to normal, still numbness in toes and fingertips without much burning. Walking without difficulty.

Starting weekly topotecan 4 mg/m2, days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days. CA-125 monthly, CT after three cycles. Given the pandemic, labs may be drawn closer to home.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video call from her kitchen, good connection.
On weekly topotecan since early March, tolerating it better than the last two. Numb toes and fingertips persist but the burning is gone and she is walking her usual loop. Staying home except for treatment because of COVID.
Home BP 124 to 132 / 76 to 82. Fasting sugars 110s to 140s, no lows.
No new symptoms.
A/P: stable chronic conditions during chemotherapy. Continue meds. Refills sent for 90 days. Labs with oncology's next draw; will add A1c to their order. Visit by video again in 3 months.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit. A1c 7.3 from last week's draw. Topotecan finishes in August; CA-125 has been falling month by month and she is cautiously hopeful.
Toes still numb, no pain. Gardening from a stool this summer.
No med changes. Visit in person in November for physical, flu earlier.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up (09/21/2020)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology
Date: 09/21/2020

Completed six cycles of weekly topotecan in August. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 09/14: resolution of the peritoneal implants, no ascites, no evidence of disease. CA-125 18 U/mL.

Plan: surveillance with exam and CA-125 every 3 months, CT yearly or for rising markers. Residual distal numbness from the vinorelbine neuropathy, stable.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Masked visit. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Waited 15 minutes in car, no reaction.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Age 56. First in-person visit since the pandemic began.
Oncology: no evidence of disease on the September CT after topotecan, CA-125 18. Every 3 month checks.
Numb toes and fingertips since February; no pain, no falls.
DM on glargine 20, A1c 7.3 in July. Thyroid stable on 112. TN quiet. RA quiet on MTX/pred.
Meds reviewed, no changes. NKDA.
PHQ-9 5: tired, some worry about scans, no hopelessness, sleeping ok.
Exam: BP 130/80. Weight 68. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, well-healed midline scar, no masses. No edema. Feet: dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses 2+; monofilament absent at the great toes and reduced at the forefoot bilaterally, vibration reduced at the toes; skin intact, no calluses.
Advance care planning: 25 minutes. She named a close friend as health care proxy, form completed; wants full treatment for now.
Plan: fasting labs today. Mammogram done 10/2019, due; order placed. Pap not needed after hysterectomy. Colonoscopy 2026. Lung screening to discuss next year. COVID vaccine when it is offered.

reports.text: Standard bilateral views. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion. Stable.
